title: Start from zero
blurb: Never written a line of code? Begin here. You learn how computers run programs, the terminal, your first language, and how web pages are made. Then you pick a direction.
outcome: You can write small programs, use Git, and build a simple web page.

stages.title: Find your feet
stages.why: The words, the terminal and the tools every developer uses daily.

stages.title: Your first language
stages.why: Python reads almost like English, so you learn programming and not punctuation.

stages.title: Your first web page
stages.why: Something you can see and show to people.

title: Frontend developer
blurb: Build what people see and touch: pages, layouts and interactive applications in the browser.
outcome: You can build a responsive, interactive web application with React and Next.js.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The web platform
stages.why: Every framework produces HTML and CSS in the end.

stages.title: JavaScript
stages.why: The language that makes pages do things.

stages.title: Applications
stages.why: Components, state and routing for real products.

title: Backend developer
blurb: Build what happens behind the screen: APIs, databases, authentication and services that stay up. In the language you choose.
outcome: You can design, build, test and ship an API with a database behind it, in a server language of your choice.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Your server language
stages.why: Pick one and learn it well. Python is the gentlest start. Java, Go, PHP, Elixir and Rust are all used for servers, and the others stay available as optional tracks.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Almost every backend is a careful way of reading and writing data.

stages.title: Services
stages.why: How an API is built, secured and tested. Taught with JavaScript and Node.js; the ideas are the same in every server language.

stages.title: Shipping
stages.why: Code is finished when it runs somewhere other than your laptop.

title: Full-stack developer
blurb: Both sides: the interface in the browser and the server and database behind it. The broadest path.
outcome: You can build and deploy a complete web application on your own.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The web platform
stages.why: Structure, style and the language of the browser.

stages.title: The interface
stages.why: Components and state.

stages.title: The server
stages.why: APIs and the database they talk to.

stages.title: The whole product
stages.why: One framework for both sides, packaged to run anywhere.

title: DevOps engineer
blurb: Get software from a commit to production, keep it running, and automate everything in between.
outcome: You can containerise a system, build its pipeline, deploy it safely and watch it in production.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: You will live in the terminal.

stages.title: A scripting language
stages.why: For everything that outgrows a shell script.

stages.title: Containers
stages.why: The unit that everything is shipped in.

stages.title: Pipelines and operations
stages.why: Build, release, deploy, observe.

stages.title: The services you will run
stages.why: Know the databases you are responsible for.

title: Database engineer
blurb: Store data so that it stays correct and comes back fast: relational, document and in-memory databases, and how to run them.
outcome: You can design a schema, write and tune queries, choose the right store for a job, and run it in containers.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: A language to script with
stages.why: Loading, checking and moving data is done with small programs.

stages.title: Relational data
stages.why: SQL is the language of data. Schema design, indexes and transactions decide whether a system is correct and fast.

stages.title: Documents and caches
stages.why: Not everything is a table. Know when a document store or an in-memory store fits better.

stages.title: Running them
stages.why: A database is a service that must be started, backed up and watched.

title: Game developer
blurb: Make things move: game loops, input, collisions and the mathematics behind them.
outcome: You can build a complete 2D game, and you understand what a game engine does for you.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Programming
stages.why: Games in the browser are written in JavaScript.

stages.title: Games
stages.why: The loop, movement, collisions, state, a finished game.

stages.title: Under the hood
stages.why: Path finding, performance, and the languages engines are written in.

title: Systems programmer
blurb: Close to the machine: memory, performance, concurrency, and the languages operating systems and databases are built in.
outcome: You understand how programs use memory and processors, in C, Rust and Go.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The machine
stages.why: C shows you memory and pointers with nothing hidden.

stages.title: Algorithms
stages.why: The difference between fast and impossible.

stages.title: Modern systems languages
stages.why: Safety without a garbage collector, and concurrency made simple.

title: AI application engineer
blurb: Build products on top of large language models: prompts, tools, agents and retrieval, with solid engineering around them.
outcome: You can build, evaluate and ship an application that uses a language model.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Python
stages.why: The language of the AI ecosystem.

stages.title: Language models
stages.why: From a first API call to agents and retrieval.

stages.title: Data and speed
stages.why: Where the documents live, and how to cache expensive calls.

stages.title: Shipping
stages.why: An API around your model, in a container.

title: Computer science foundations
blurb: The core of a computer science course, and of technical interviews: a language, how the machine works, data structures and algorithms.
outcome: You can reason about memory and running time, and solve algorithm problems in the language you chose.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: A language to think in
stages.why: Pick one. The algorithm exercises accept any of them.

stages.title: The machine
stages.why: C shows what a program really does with memory. It explains the rest.

stages.title: Data structures and algorithms
stages.why: From Big-O to graphs and dynamic programming.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Nearly every program stores something. SQL is asked about in most interviews.

title: Python developer
blurb: One language for scripts, servers, data and AI. The gentlest way in, and it goes a long way.
outcome: You can write, test and ship Python programs that use databases and language models.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Python
stages.why: From the first function to classes, generators, testing and typing.

stages.title: Problem solving
stages.why: Data structures and algorithms turn knowing a language into being able to solve problems with it.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Real programs keep their data in a database.

stages.title: Building with it
stages.why: Language models are where Python is used most today. Docker gets your program onto a server.

title: Java developer
blurb: The language of large business systems, banks and Android: strict types, objects, and a huge ecosystem.
outcome: You can design a Java program with classes, interfaces and collections, back it with a database, and package it in a container.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Java
stages.why: Types, classes, interfaces, collections, generics, exceptions and streams.

stages.title: Data structures and algorithms
stages.why: Java interviews lean on them heavily. Solve the exercises in Java.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Almost every Java service talks to a relational database, and often to a cache.

stages.title: Services
stages.why: How systems are packaged, split into services and kept running.

title: Go developer
blurb: The language of cloud software: small, fast, and built for servers and command-line tools.
outcome: You can build a concurrent Go service with an HTTP API and a database, and ship and operate it.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Go
stages.why: Slices, maps, structs, interfaces, errors, goroutines and channels, and an HTTP API.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: A service is usually a thin layer over its data.

stages.title: Containers and services
stages.why: Go and containers grew up together: Docker itself is written in Go.

stages.title: Operations
stages.why: Pipelines, deployment and monitoring: where much Go is written.

title: Rust developer
blurb: The speed and control of C, with a compiler that proves your memory is used safely.
outcome: You can write safe, fast Rust with ownership, traits and iterators, and you know what it protects you from.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The machine
stages.why: Rust's rules make sense once you have seen, in C, the problems they prevent.

stages.title: Rust
stages.why: Ownership and borrowing, enums and match, Option and Result, traits, iterators.

stages.title: Data structures and algorithms
stages.why: Building them in Rust is the real test of understanding ownership.

stages.title: Around the code
stages.why: Scripts and containers, to build and ship what you write.

title: Elixir developer
blurb: Functional programming on the Erlang virtual machine: many small processes, and systems that keep running when parts fail.
outcome: You can write Elixir with pattern matching, processes and GenServers, and build a service that recovers from failure.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Elixir
stages.why: Pattern matching, recursion, pipes, processes, GenServer, Mix and ExUnit.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Elixir applications keep their state in a database and share fast data through a cache.

stages.title: Systems that stay up
stages.why: Containers, several services working together, and what to do when one of them fails.

title: PHP web developer
blurb: The language behind WordPress, Wikipedia and Laravel: pages, forms and APIs backed by a database.
outcome: You can build a web application in PHP with forms, a JSON API and a database, and put it in a container.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The web platform
stages.why: PHP produces HTML. Know what it has to produce.

stages.title: PHP
stages.why: Arrays, functions, classes, requests and forms, JSON APIs, and databases with PDO.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Nearly every PHP application sits on a relational database.

stages.title: In the browser
stages.why: JavaScript makes the pages you serve interactive.

stages.title: Shipping
stages.why: Package the application and its database so that it runs anywhere.

title: Vue developer
blurb: Interactive applications in the browser with Vue: single-file components, reactivity and composables.
outcome: You can build an interactive Vue application and connect it to an API.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The web platform
stages.why: Vue templates are HTML, and components are styled with CSS.

stages.title: JavaScript
stages.why: Vue is JavaScript. The better you know the language, the less the framework surprises you.

stages.title: Vue
stages.why: Components, reactivity, props and events, lists, forms and composables.

stages.title: A server behind it
stages.why: An application needs an API to talk to.
